doc.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013

chapter: Rock and roll, Elvis and Sinatra
title: Mama Thornton's Hound Dog versus Elvis
summary: A blindfold clip of Big Mama Thornton, comparing it with Elvis's version and meaning.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And you know when Elvis did it, he did a great job, but it was a whole different thing. You know, he isn’t singing about the same thing she’s singing about.

I just think it’s so — you know this is a different recording than another one I had because she actually, the music actually gets turned around, the beat. Or she comes in, you know, the 12-bar form gets a little askew, the way she’s singing it. But you know what, it doesn’t matter at all.
She’s like, Big Mama, do what you wanna do.
I like, what’s his name, “Bear Cat” The answer song that Thomas did.
Yeah. See Elvis of course, he’s singing about a little hound dog you know, and playing with the little doggie thing.
Yeah, with the little hat on.
Great interpretation, taking it a whole different way. You know it has nothing to do with what she was singing about.
